# Review of beowulf-fitt-09 (lines 559–661) — pass 1 of 2

Reviewer pass on `units.json` (39 units). `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` verified byte-identical to the drafter's file by script before and after; JSON valid (indent 1, round-trips). 37 units changed, 86 change entries. Order followed: (1) labels, positions, apparatus abbreviations; (2) Old English to `l` word by word; (3) `l` to `i`; (4) remembered English in `i`; (5) published renderings (fitt-01 to fitt-08 grepped: eorl, gedriht, lāð, ǣglǣca, aldre þīnum, nīpende niht, wado weallende, brytta, gamol, maþelode).

Totals: **high 3, medium 40, low 43.**

Apparatus policy applied: only the packet is evidence. Abbreviations the packet does not expand (`Gru.`, `Gru.tr.`, `Gr.1`, `Gr. Bibl.`, `Holtzm.`, `Kal.`, `Arn.`, `Cos.`, `He.-Soc.`, `E.Sc.`, siglum `A`) are now quoted as printed. Kept as expansions because earlier fitts fixed them: `Ke.` Kemble, `Tho.`/`Thk.` Thorkelin, `Tr.` Trautmann, `Holt.` Holthausen, `Sed.` Sedgefield, `Klu.` Kluge, `Schü.` Schücking, `Cha.` Chambers, `Bu.` Bugge, `Rie.` Rieger, `B.-T.` Bosworth–Toller.

### High

- **565 · n · high.** note first said the subject of letton is brimlīðende, then that the monsters are the subject and brimlīðende the object; also said lettan "takes the dative, so lāde is the dative" while treating the participle as object. Done: one consistent parse: monsters subject, brimlīðende object, lāde dative of respect.
- **646 · i · high.** i rendered oþðe as "until" (and reversed the structure), l kept "or"; the note said it took oþðe "as until", which the apparatus does not support (until is "Gru." oð þæt); "monster" vs published "fearsome one". Done: i now follows l ("or"); note rewritten; "fearsome one".
- **646 · n · high.** note said oþðe was taken as "until" in i (not supported: until is Gru.'s oð þæt); hilde called a dative though it is the noun of the participle phrase (accusative); "Thorkelin and four later editions" omitted E.Sc.; Grundtvig attribution from memory; "at the high hall" for tō. Done: rewritten end to end; every label re-derived from the line.

## Findings considered and refused (with reasons)

- **562 · "Næs" as plain "not".** The shared glossary entry says "ne wæs — contraction"; the note says it works as "not" before ‘hæfdon’ and flags it as a reading from the sense. Left: the note is honest and `l` ("Not they") is right either way.
- **565 · ford = strait.** Left as the note's own flagged guess; only the `i` word "deep" was wrong and is fixed.
- **569 · swaþredon "subside".** Left: rare verb, already called a guess in the note.
- **574 · accepting ābrēat or mēce.** Refused: Klaeber's text stands; the note says the sense is the same.
- **583 · [fela] versus [geflites].** Left as Klaeber prints; note states both.
- **586/643 · whether the dash and parenthesis in `i` are legitimate.** Left: Klaeber prints the dashes.
- **598 · the crux itself (wigeð, swefeð, sendeþ).** Not re-decided. `l` "bears lust, puts to sleep and sends" and `i` "takes his pleasure, kills and sends (them off)" are both flagged in the note as low-confidence; the parenthetical "(them off)" is the drafter's supply and the note says so. Left, because every alternative in the apparatus is worse supported and the convention is to render plainly and say the reading is disputed. A QUESTIONS.md entry is still owed (see below).
- **598 · "bears lust" for lust wigeð.** Left: wegan is the Klaeber/glossary-grounded parse, and the note names Kemble's and Bugge's alternatives.
- **599–601 · "ic" cancelled by editors.** Not applied; Klaeber keeps it.
- **612 · "mindful of what was due to her kin" in `i`.** A guess already flagged in the note; `l` "mindful of kin" is literal. Left.
- **618 · whole unit.** Checked word by word, no change needed.
- **628 · circumflex on Wealhþeôn explained as "contracted vowel".** Matches the conventions file. Left.
- **640 · "to sit by her lord" for tō hire frēan sittan.** Left: tō … sittan "to sit (beside)" is natural and the note says "to sit".
- **646 · inserting [ne] or reading oþðe as "until" in the text of the translation.** Refused: Klaeber prints neither; both appear only in the note.
- **646 · "shadow-helmed shapes" in `i`.** A rendering of an obscure genitive compound; the note now says it is a guess at a picture of dusk. Kept, not replaced by a smoother invented phrase.
- **655 · "mighty house" for þrȳþærn.** Considered as an echo risk; it is two plain words built from þrȳþ and ærn and the note unpacks the compound. Left.
- **658 · "Take now and keep" for Hafa nū ond geheald.** Left: plain, and "have" alone would be stiff.
- **578/581/583 · `l` word order.** Left where English can bear it.
- **560 · "grim humour" in the note.** Interpretive but hedged by the surrounding sentences. Left.
- **588 · "flat future" for scealt.** Left: a reasonable label for the sense, stated as such.
- **611 · Tr. cancels wǣron.** Kept; `Tr.` is Trautmann by the earlier fitt findings.

# Pass 2 (adversarial re-read, 2026-10-12)

Fresh full pass on `units.json` (39 units) and on the glosser's `gloss.json` (227 new entries and 40 broadenings at the start of the pass; one broadening added). Order followed: (1) grammatical labels in the notes against the form and position in the line; (2) Old English to `l` word by word; (3) `l` to `i`; (4) remembered English in `i`; (5) consistency with published renderings (fitt-01 to fitt-08 grepped: ǣglǣca/āglǣca, nīpende niht, wado weallende, hūsa sēlest, Beorht-Dena/brego, tō banan, aldre þīnum, eorl, gedriht, maþelode, duguþe ond geogoþe, wyrd, ellen). Cross-references in the notes (lines 34, 117, 146, 147, 160, 285, 427, 504, 508, 513, 523, 525, 526, 530, 532, 541, 547, 555, 570, 1870, 2516) were checked against `source/beowulf-klaeber1922.json` and the published parts. `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` verified unchanged by script; JSON round-trips with the same formatting (indent 1, no ASCII escaping); no backticks in any note or glossary entry. All 41 broadenings (40 + 1 added) were checked against `beowulf-glossary.json`: each old part is the root entry whole, followed by " · ".

Totals: **high 0, medium 8, low 26** (34 changes: 18 in `units.json`, 16 in `gloss.json`).

## Changes in units.json (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

### Medium

- **590 · n · medium.** said `gefremede` is "a past subjunctive in the main clause"; the 3rd singular past ends the same in both moods, so the label is not true of the form alone. Done: states the form is mood-neutral, the unreal sense comes from the `gif` clause, and only `wǣre` is a clear subjunctive.
- **590 · n · medium.** note said `ealdre þīnum` is "to your prince" while `l` has "to your chief" (published fitt-05 344) and the next sentence says "chief, lord". Done: "to your chief".

- **632 · n · medium.** called `geworhte` "a past subjunctive"; 1st singular past ends the same in both moods (unlike `crunge`, which is a true subjunctive form and was left). Done: hedged as above.

## Re-read of the passages pass 1 rewrote on judgment

- **565.** Parse is now consistent: monsters subject of `letton`, `brimlīðende` object (nominative and accusative look alike, said so), `lāde` dative, `ford` = strait a flagged guess. `l` and `i` follow it. The siglum "A" is quoted as printed and hedged. No fault left except the two low items above.
- **598-601.** Labels true: `nymeð` 3sg, `ārað` takes the dative, `lēode Deniga` genitive in the odd form, `wigeð` from `wegan`, `swefeð` two possible verbs, `sendeþ` without an object, `wēneþ` with genitive or accusative, `tō Gār-Denum` dative after `tō`. Every apparatus attribution (Ke., Bu., Tho., Arn., B.-T., Gru., Gru.tr., E., Holt., Tr., Sed., He.-Soc., Holtzm., Gr. Bibl.) is as printed in the packet; the unexplained "o. s." is declared as such. `l` "bears lust, puts to sleep and sends" and `i` "takes his pleasure, kills and sends (them off)" agree with the note, which calls both low-confidence. - **620-621.** `ymbēode` takes the accusative, so `dǣl ǣghwylcne` is the object and `duguþe ond geogoþe` genitives; the note names the datives-or-accusatives alternative and calls the construction loose. `l` follows the Old English order, `i` and note agree. 160 is the right cross-reference (checked in the source). The apparatus is quoted exactly as the packet gives it: 648b "E.Sc., Tho., 4 Edd. insert [ne]", 649a "Ke., et al., 4 Edd. opðe; Gru.tr. 276, Gru. oð þæt", 643 Sedgefield's transposition with the MPh. reference. ## Findings considered and refused (with reasons)

- **620 · i "ripe in mind" against `l` and note "thriven in mind".** Refused: `i` may use a natural English word for `geþungen`; the note gives the literal gloss.
- **636 · i "meet my last day" as a possible echo.** Refused: built from `gebīdan` (await, undergo) and `endedæg`; "last day" is plain English and pass 1 already moved off "live to see".
- **632 · i "wholly fulfill your people's wish, or fall in the slaughter".** Refused: each phrase maps to a word of the line; no fully formed phrase of a published translation is recalled.
- **655-660 · i "mighty house", "remember your renown, show your strength and valor, keep watch against the foe".** Refused: unpacked from `þrȳþærn`, `mǣrþo`, `mægenellen cȳð`, `waca wið wrāþum`; "foe" for `wrāþum` is the plain choice, and the line-by-line shape follows the Old English imperatives.
- **590 · i "terrible fearsome one".** Refused: both words are published (atol, fitt-02 164; ǣglǣca "fearsome one"); redundant but literal.
- **559 · lāð "hateful" against fitt-08 "loathed".** Refused: fitt-08 renders the adjective in `nē lēof nē lāð` and `wið lāðum`; here `lāðgetēona` is an active compound ("hateful injurer"), and fitt-01/02 use "hateful". No single house rendering exists.
- **575 · "on niht" attached to the fighter in `i` ("by night").** Refused: the note says so; the order of the line allows it.
- **607/643 · gloss `sǣl` gender "masculine" for the joy sense.** Not changed: cannot be settled from the packet or the lexica allowed by the packet.
- **cynna (known entry "of kinds, races")** for `cynna gemyndig`. Not broadened: the entry's form label is true; the sense "kin" is the note's.
- **Note length.** Several notes (598, 646, 583, 652) exceed 150 words; the validator only warns. Left: the cruces need the space.
